item.title: Yoshida Fire Festival: Giant Torches Marking Fuji's Climbing Season Close — Guide
item.description: The Yoshida Fire Festival, held each late August in Fujiyoshida, is one of Japan’s three most unusual festivals, traditionally marking the close of Mount Fuji’s climbing season with a dramatic display of fire. On the main evening, dozens of giant torches, some three metres tall, are lit along the town’s main street alongside smaller fires outside homes and shops, filling the streets with flame and smoke as portable shrines are paraded through, in a centuries-old ritual tied to the Sengen shrine and Fuji worship, praying for safety on the mountain.
